In the United States, it participated for the first time in logistics real estate development and detached housing sales businesses; it also newly entered the housing sales business in India, and in addition to ASEAN countries, it continues housing sales in Australia and Canada.

In the fiscal year ended March 2026, which marked the 90th anniversary of the team's founding, the Hanshin Tigers won the league championship for the first time in two years and advanced through the Climax Series to the Japan Series. The seating capacity of Hanshin Koshien Stadium is 47,359. In January 2026, the company opened “THE SUMO LIVE RESTAURANT Nichirakuza GINZA TOKYO,” a show restaurant for inbound visitors themed on sumo and Japanese cuisine.

Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥106,393 million. Revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥106,472 million (up 1.7% year on year), as air transport handling recovered in Japan, China and ASEAN and business remained solid. The company made INTERNATIONAL CARGO EXPRESS PTY LTD., which has strengths in international transport in Australia, a subsidiary, and established a local subsidiary in Bangladesh. It has also strengthened its logistics business by expanding logistics warehouses in South Africa and Mexico.

entries.85dc3bf2cfc116c2: This category is operated by Hankyu Corporation, Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd., Nose Electric Railway Co., Ltd., Kita-Osaka Kyuko Electric Railway Co., Ltd., and Kobe Kōsoku Tetsudō Co., Ltd.; operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥160,316 million (up 4.5% year on year). For the fiscal year ended March 2026, Hankyu Corporation had an operating distance of 143.6 km, passenger volume of 628,643 thousand (up 3.2%), and total transport revenue of ¥104,444 million (up 4.0%). Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd. had an operating distance of 48.9 km, passenger volume of 254,326 thousand (up 4.9%), and total revenue of ¥40,132 million (up 5.1%). In August 2025, Hankyu Corporation increased the number of trains operating on its reserved-seat service “PRiVACE” by about 1.5 times, and Hanshin Electric Railway is manufacturing new rolling stock in preparation for introducing a reserved-seat service in spring 2027. It has been advancing the installation of platform screen doors and other facilities, and has started one-person operation on the Hankyu Minoo Line.
entries.8809e9f9653d7c7d: This category owns and leases office buildings, commercial facilities and logistics facilities, and also includes property management and building maintenance businesses and real estate fund and REIT businesses. The business descriptions table lists Hankyu Corporation, Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd., Hankyu Hanshin Properties Co., Ltd., Hankyu Hanshin Building Management Co., Ltd., Hankyu Hanshin Clean Service Co., Ltd., and Hankyu Hanshin REIT Management Co., Ltd. Operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥196,814 million (up 6.8% year on year). In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it advanced renewals of “NU Chayamachi” (Kita Ward, Osaka) and “Rosavia” (Ibaraki, Osaka Prefecture), began new construction on the “(Tentative name) Higashi Hankyu Building Reconstruction Project” (Kita Ward, Osaka), and completed “Ensuite Onarimon,” a medium-sized renovated office in Minato Ward, Tokyo. New construction began on the logistics facilities “Logista Osaka Yodogawa” and “Logista Kyoto Fushimi,” and construction of the “Grand Green Osaka” project, the Umekita Phase 2 area development project, is proceeding as planned toward the full opening of the district in fiscal 2027.
entries.8bda1dbe64b8bc8a: This reportable segment comprises the railway, automobile and distribution businesses; its core companies are Hankyu Corporation and Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥209,018 million, the third largest among the reportable segments. Operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥214,293 million (up 4.4% year on year), as railway passenger volume increased due to the Osaka-Kansai Expo and expanding inbound demand. From the current fiscal year, some subsidiaries of the urban transportation segment are presented within the “Other” segment, and figures for the previous year have been reclassified for comparison.

entries.8f9211bb0801af96: Under its Long-term Management Vision formulated in March 2025, the company aims to close the gap between its desired future state, targeted for around 2040, and its current situation. Its business strategy sets four directions: realizing an overwhelming No.1 presence along its rail lines, maximizing the appeal of its content and developing new content, expanding beyond its area (Greater Tokyo Area and overseas), and focusing on business solutions; it states that it will continue to deepen existing fields centered on its rail lines and take on challenges in new fields with expected growth. Under its financial strategy, the Urban Transportation Business and the Real Estate Leasing and Development Business stably generate funds that are channeled into growth businesses; it positions the Real Estate Business (Global), Housing Business, Hotel Business, Information Services Business and Travel Business, among others, as playing a role in driving group growth. Under its human resources strategy, it states that it will secure diverse and capable personnel, deploy them in growth areas, and systematically develop personnel to lead the future.

Operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥48,110 million (up 7.3% year on year). Its core company is Hankyu Hanshin Properties Co., Ltd. Hankyu Corporation and Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd. are also responsible for the leasing and other businesses and the housing business. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥396,184 million, the largest among the reportable segments. Operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥406,705 million (up 10.6% year on year), with condominium sales revenue rising significantly. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥55,778 million, and revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥71,968 million (up 2.7% year on year). In the information services business, results were strong, driven by growth in internet-related businesses such as e-commerce and orders for the transport terminal operation system at the Osaka-Kansai Expo. In the broadcasting and telecommunications business, the company provides FTTH services (high-speed internet services using optical fiber) and has also received orders from local governments for projects such as ICT environment development at elementary and junior high schools. In the safety and education business, the number of schools and facilities introducing “Tōkōkō Mimamorume” increased, and the company operates the robot programming school “Puroguraboo.”

Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥295,768 million, the second largest among the reportable segments after the real estate business. Operating revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥296,546 million (up 13.6% year on year). In overseas travel, handling of long-haul tours led by Europe increased, and domestic travel also performed steadily through early tour sales and an expanded product lineup. Inbound travel to Japan saw strong tour sales against the backdrop of rising inbound demand; in addition to undertaking transport support work for the Osaka-Kansai Expo, it is actively winning solutions business orders from local governments.
